claims.statement: The LangGraph deployment manifest registers the agent, reviewer, and review-scout graphs with the FastAPI application `openswe.webapp:app`, loads `.env`, installs custom auth, and configures checkpoint deletion with a 60-minute sweep and 43,200-minute default TTL.
`make dev` starts the local Postgres dependency when `POSTGRES_URI` is absent, rejects an occupied port 2024, and runs `uv run langgraph dev --no-browser --port 2024 --n-jobs-per-worker 10`.
`make run` runs `uvicorn openswe.webapp:app --reload --port 8000`, providing the FastAPI app without the LangGraph runtime; run-creating operations therefore require `make dev`.
`make install` installs Python development dependencies with `uv sync --extra dev`, while the Makefile provides uv-based pytest, Ruff, and ty targets for tests, formatting/linting, and type checking.

The project requires Python 3.14+, constrains local Agent Server dependencies to `langgraph-api>=0.16.0,<0.17` and `langgraph-runtime-inmem>=0.36.0,<0.37`, while `langgraph.json` targets an `>~=0.15.0rc1` API manifest and the root image uses `langgraph-api:0.15.1-py3.14`.
The pnpm workspace includes bridge-client, ui, desktop, cli, and tests/e2e; root build, check, test, and typecheck scripts delegate to Turborepo.

`make web` runs the dashboard development task, whose dev proxy targets `DASHBOARD_API_URL` and defaults to `http://localhost:2024`; `make dev-ui` concurrently starts Vite and the backend with `DASHBOARD_DEV_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:3000`.
The dashboard workspace's build, check, test, and typecheck scripts fan out through Turborepo, while root lint and formatting scripts invoke oxlint and oxfmt directly.
Turborepo caches `.output/**`, `.vercel/output/**`, and `build/**` for builds and includes backend URL, source commit, Vercel, E2E, and `VITE_*` environment inputs in relevant task hashes.

The experimental Electron desktop client packages the compiled dashboard, requires a user-selected compatible backend rather than a hosted default, and supports This Mac sandbox execution through a bridge that long-polls the backend and returns results.

`make install-desktop` refuses a dirty checkout, fast-forwards `main`, and invokes `scripts/install_desktop.sh`, whereas `make install-checkout` invokes that installer against the current checkout without changing Git state.
`scripts/install_desktop.sh` is macOS-only, requires Node, `ditto`, Bun, and pnpm or Corepack, builds a packed desktop app, then stages and swaps it into `/Applications` or `~/Applications`.

`scripts/create_sandbox_snapshot.py` uses `SandboxClient` to build a LangSmith sandbox snapshot from a Docker image, prints its ID, and directs operators to choose it as a workspace base snapshot in the dashboard.

`scripts/purge_wakeup_crons.py` is a one-time cleanup for expired `thread_wakeup` crons; it resolves a deployment from `--url` or `LANGGRAPH_URL`, uses `LANGGRAPH_API_KEY` or `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`, and supports `--dry-run`.

The root Dockerfile builds the standalone Agent Server backend image from `langchain/langgraph-api:0.15.1-py3.14`, installs the checkout with API constraints, configures the HTTP app, checkpoint TTL, and three graph registrations, and exposes port 8000.

A standalone backend requires Agent Server backing settings including `DATABASE_URI`, `REDIS_URI`, `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`, and `LANGGRAPH_CLOUD_LICENSE_KEY`, must publish a public `LANGGRAPH_URL`, and should not use scale-to-zero hosting because background work relies on Redis/Postgres-backed workers.

`ui/Dockerfile` is a multi-stage Node 24 Alpine build run from the repository root; it performs a frozen filtered pnpm install, builds the dashboard into Nitro `.output`, and serves it as user `node` on port 8080.

The production Nitro proxy reads `DASHBOARD_API_URL` at request time and throws when it is unset; it preserves path, query, method, streamed body, individual cookies, and manual OAuth redirects while filtering transport headers.

The FastAPI app rejects wildcard `DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` because it enables credentialed CORS, allows the Electron `open-swe://app` origin, and installs dashboard, webhook, health, and other custom routers before mounting the dashboard UI.

The backend serves a built dashboard from `DASHBOARD_STATIC_DIR` or `ui/.output/public`, or proxies a configured Vite dev server; its UI catch-all declines reserved API and LangGraph paths, serves only HTML navigations for unknown paths, and gives hashed assets immutable caching.

A bundled dashboard must be built with `DASHBOARD_BASE_PATH` matching the LangGraph `http.mount_prefix`; the platform manifest derives that value from `langgraph.json`, while local `make build-dashboard` callers must supply it for a prefixed mount.
`make tunnel` requires `NGROK_DOMAIN` and exposes local port 2024 through an ngrok policy that returns 404 outside `/webhooks/*`, avoiding publication of unauthenticated local LangGraph routes.

The root backend Dockerfile does not build the dashboard, so standalone serving needs a prebuilt dashboard or `DASHBOARD_STATIC_DIR`; in contrast, the platform manifest performs a best-effort dashboard build and continues deployment if it fails.

A standalone deployment using `LANGGRAPH_AUTH_TYPE=noop` leaves raw LangGraph routes exposed to reachable clients; operators must use LangSmith auth or a private/authenticated network boundary because dashboard sessions and webhook signatures cover only custom routes.

The FastAPI lifespan validates login, sandbox, local-model, MDA, and PostgreSQL configuration; runs database migrations before starting workers; and stops workers, listeners, the HTTP pool, and database resources during shutdown, while several ancillary listeners and warmup failures degrade with warnings rather than aborting startup.

New agent, reviewer, and review-scout threads are claimed for the Managed Deep Agents runtime; the backend forwards their runs, state, history, stream, and cancellation operations there, and the backend refuses startup without MDA configuration.

Open SWE application migrations are stored under `openswe/database/migrations`, use the `open_swe` PostgreSQL schema, and `make migration m="..."` creates a numbered Alembic revision chained to all current migration heads.
